topic: Synchronize abstract with historical and prospective results while retaining adverse evidence
old: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) in law must trace multi-hop precedent chains and must not present overruled doctrine as current law, yet common evaluators reward entity overlap rather than grounded reasoning. We introduce TERRA, an experimental dual-phase GraphRAG architecture. Offline, it builds an Event Evolution Graph over \CorpusTotalOpinions\ Supreme Court opinions connected by \CorpusPrecedentEdges\ directed citation edges, plus an index of generic procedural scaffolds. Online, a small-model Traffic Cop router sends single-point lookups down a lighter fast path (retrieval and an entailment check, without graph traversal) and multi-hop questions through citation traversal, and an LLM-prompted entailment grader evaluates retrieved evidence before generation. We evaluate on a \numUniqueQueries-query benchmark against four baselines (\numTotalEvals\ evaluations) using two non-Llama judges, paired Wilcoxon tests and Benjamini--Hochberg correction. TERRA scores higher overall faithfulness ($\TerraOverallFaithfulnessMean$ vs.\ $\HippoRAGOverallFaithfulnessMean$ for the next best system, overlapping 95\% CIs) and answer-only faithfulness ($\TerraAnswerOnlyFaithfulnessMean$, computed on differing answered subsets), and significantly outperforms all three retrieval baselines on Category~B multi-hop reasoning ($\Delta$ from $\CatBTerraVsHippoRAGDelta$ [HippoRAG] and $\CatBTerraVsFlatDelta$ [Flat] to $\CatBTerraVsGraphRAGDelta$ [GraphRAG]; FDR $q<0.05$; Flat CI includes zero), although a no-retrieval Direct LLM scores significantly higher on Category~B ($\Delta=\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMDelta$, $q=\CatBTerraVsDirectLLMAdjQ$; TERRA's Category~B faithfulness is low in absolute terms, $\TerraCatBFaithfulness$). On adversarial Category~D queries TERRA safely handles \TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate\ of traps (\TerraCatDRejectionRate\ explicit refusals, \TerraCatDRefutationRate\ verified refutations) with \TerraCatDFatalErrors\ fatal errors, but refuses \TerraCatAFalseRefusals\ Category~A and \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries, at \TerraLatencyMedianSeconds~s median latency. On \ObscCohortSize\ obscure overruled precedents, Direct LLM safe handling falls to \ObscDirectSafePct\ versus \ObscFullSafePct\ for full TERRA, but TERRA without curated overruling labels drops to \ObscUnlabeledSafePct, not significantly different from flat retrieval ($p\,\ObscPrimaryMcNemarPRel$); safety depends on curated annotations. Absent licensed attorney evaluation, human review remains an essential deployment prerequisite.
new: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for historical law must retrieve connected authorities without treating overruled doctrine as current law. We introduce TERRA, an experimental GraphRAG pipeline combining an Event Evolution Graph over \CorpusTotalOpinions\ Supreme Court opinions, generic five-step procedural scaffolds, EASY/HARD routing and LLM-prompted evidence checking. Its scaffolds are not case-specific judicial reasoning. A historical \numUniqueQueries-query, five-system evaluation uses two non-Llama judges and paired tests with Benjamini--Hochberg correction. TERRA's Category~B faithfulness exceeds the retrieval baselines but remains below Direct LLM; its overall and answer-only scores describe different refusal and answered subsets. Adversarial safe handling is \TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate, with \TerraCatDFatalErrors\ fatal errors and false refusals on \TerraCatAFalseRefusals\ Category~A and \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries. The obscure-precedent advantage depends on curated overruling annotations. A separate prospective comparison evaluates graph retrieval (T) against dense--BM25 retrieval (H) on the same 350 queries with shared evidence budgets, verification, generation and judges. On 100 Category~B pairs, mean evidence faithfulness is 0.76400 for T and 0.49515 for H (paired difference 0.26885; bootstrap 95\% CI [0.16035, 0.37205]; randomization $p\approx0.000010$). T triggers 69/100 verifier refusals versus H's 4/100: the gain concerns the gated pipeline, not demonstrated answer coverage or legal correctness. External and temporal evaluations remain mixed. Historical configuration gaps, annotation dependence and absent licensed-practitioner validation restrict the findings to an experimental research framework.
